See The NORB dataset for generic object recognition is [available for download](http://www.cs.nyu.edu/~ylclab/data/norb-v1.0).![Image 7: A collection of toy figures, including a plane, a car, an animal, and a human figure, are arranged together](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/images/norb-sample-01.png) [**CLICK HERE FOR MORE INFORMATION, PICTURES, PAPERS >>>>>**](http://www.cs.nyu.edu/~yann/research/norb). Tired of Matlab? [Lush](http://lush.sourceforge.net/) is an easy-to-learn, open-source **object-oriented programming language** designed for researchers, experimenters, and engineers working in **large-scale numerical and graphic applications**. Lush combines three languages in one: a very simple to use, loosely-typed interpreted language, a strongly-typed compiled language with the same syntax, and the C language, which can be freely mixed with the other languages within a single source file, and even within a single function. [![Image 8: Green background with the word Lush on top and a small image of a frog in water below](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/images/lush-logo-03-138x102.png)](http://lush.sourceforge.net/) Lush has a library of over 14,000 functions and classes, some of which are simple interfaces to popular libraries: vector/matrix/tensor algebra, linear algebra (LAPACK, BLAS), numerical function (GSL), 2D and 3D graphics (X, SDL, OpenGL, OpenRM, PostScipt), image processing, computer vision (OpenCV), machine learning (gblearning, Torch), regular expressions, audio processing (ALSA), and video grabbing (Video4linux). If you do research and development in **signal processing, image processing, machine learning, computer vision, bio-informatics, data mining, statistics, or artificial intelligence**, and feel limited by Matlab and other existing tools, **Lush** is for you. If you want a simple environment to experiment with **graphics, video, and sound**, Lush is for you. Lush is Free Software (GPL) and runs under GNU/Linux, Solaris, and Irix. [**VISIT THE LUSH HOME PAGE >>>>**](http://lush.sourceforge.net/) ![Image 9: DjVuLibre](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/images/djvu_badge-140x49.gif)![Image 10: An old book page in French titled DICTIONAIRE PHARMACEUTIQUE AUGMENTE DE NOUVEAV](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/images/pharm-thumb.jpeg) My main research topic until I left AT&T was the [DjVu](http://www.djvuzone.org/home.html) project. DjVu is a document format, a set of compression methods and a software platform for distributing scanned and digitally produced documents on the Web. DjVu image files of scanned documents are typically 3-8 times smaller than PDF or TIFF-groupIV for bitonal and 5-10 times smaller than PDF or JPEG for color (at 300 DPI). DjVu versions of digitally produced documents are more compact and render much faster than the PDF or PostScript versions. [Hundreds of websites around the world](http://www.djvuzone.org/links/index.html) are using DjVu for Web-based and CDROM-based document repositories and digital libraries. * [Yann's DjVu page](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/djvu/index.html): a description of DjVu, and a set of useful links. * [Technical talk on DjVu](http://www.cs.uiuc.edu/news/dls/distlectpst.html): watch a streaming video of Yann's Distinguished Lecture at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, October 22 2001. [(100K Windows Streaming Media)](http://a.cs.uiuc.edu/dls/dls0102/dls0102-lecun-high.asx). [(56K Windows Streaming Media)](http://a.cs.uiuc.edu/dls/dls0102/dls0102-lecun-low.asx), * [DjVuZone.org](http://www.djvuzone.org/index.html): samples, demos, technical information, papers, and tutorials on DjVu.... DjVuZone hosts several digital libraries, including [NIPS Online](http://nips.djvuzone.org/). * [DjVuLibre for Unix](http://djvu.sourceforge.net/): free/open-source browser plug-ins, viewers, utilites, and libraries for Unix. * [Commercial DjVu Software](http://www.djvu.com/): free plug-ins for Windows and Mac, free and commercial applications for Windows and some Unix platforms (hosted at [LizardTech](http://www.lizardtech.com/), the company that distributes and supports DjVu under license from AT&T). * [Any2DjVu](http://any2djvu.djvuzone.org/) and [Bib2Web](http://bib2web.djvuzone.org/): Upload your documents and get them converted to DjVu. Bib2Web automates the creation of [publication pages](http://bib2web.djvuzone.org/sample-output/publis.html) for researchers. ![Image 11: The image shows various examples of the number 23, and a snippet of code related to LeNet 5 research](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/images/a23-small.gif) My main research interest is machine learning, particularly how it applies to perception, and more particularly to visual perception. I am currently working on two architectures for gradient-based perceptual learning: **graph transformer networks** and **convolutional networks.** Convolutional Nets are a special kind of neural net architecture designed to recognize images directly from pixel data. Convolutional Nets can be trained to detect, segment and recognize objects with excellent robustness to noise, and variations of position, scale, angle, and shape. Have a look at the animated [demonstrations of LeNet-5](http://yann.lecun.com/exdb/lenet/index.html), a Convolutional Nets trained to recognize handwritten digit strings. Convolutional nets and graph transformer networks are embedded in several high speed scanners used by banks to read checks. A system I helped develop reads an estimated **10 percent of all the checks written in the US**. Check out [this page](http://yann.lecun.com/exdb/lenet/index.html), and/or read [this paper](http://yann.lecun.com/exdb/publis/index.html#lecun-98) to learn more about Convolutional Nets and graph transformer networks. The [MNIST database](http://yann.lecun.com/exdb/mnist/index.html) contains 60,000 training samples and 10,000 test samples of size-normalized handwritten digits. This database was derived from the original NIST databases. MNIST is widely used by researchers as a benchmark for testing pattern recognition methods, and by students for class projects in pattern recognition, machine learning, and statistics. I have several interests beside my family (my wife and three sons) and my research: * [Playing Music](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/music/index.html): particularly Jazz, Renaissance and Baroque music. A few MP3 and MIDI files of Renaissance music are [available here](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/music/index.html). * [Building and flying miniature flying contraptions](http://www.lecun.org/hobby/planes.html): preferably battery powered, radio controled, and unconventional in their design. ![Image 12: Man holding a white toy plane in front of a grassy field and a blue sky](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/images/plane01-thumb.jpg) * Building robots: particularly Lego robots (before the days of the Lego Mindstorms) * Hacking various computing equipment: I have owned 5 computers between 1978 and 1992: SYM-1, OSI C2-4P, Commodore 64, Amiga 1000, Amiga 4000. then I lost interest in personal computing when the only thing you could get was a boring Wintel box. Then, Linux appeared and I came back to life..... * Sailing: I own two sport catamarans, a Nacra 5.8 and a Prindle 19. I also sail and race larger boats with friends. * Graphic Design: I designed the DjVu logo and much of the AT&T DjVu web site. * Reading European comics. Comics in certain European countries (France, Belgium, Italy, Spain) are considered a true art form ("le 8-ieme art"), and not just a business with products targeted at teenagers like on this side of the pond. Although I don't have a shred of evidence to support it, I claim to have the largest private collection of French-language comics in the Eastern US. * making bad puns in French, but I don't have much of an audience this side of the pond. * Sipping wine, particularly red, particularly French, particularly Bordeaux, particularly Saint-Julien. [![Image 13: Bib2Web](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/images/b2w-80x40.gif)](http://bib2web.djvuzone.org/) No deep science here, but if you are looking for a simple/automatic way to make all your publications (digital or paper-based) available on your web page, visit [Bib2Web](http://bib2web.djvuzone.org/). * [Photos taken at various conferences, workshops, trade shows and other professional events](http://www.lecun.org/gallery/libpro/index.html). Includes pictures from CVPR, NIPS, Learning@Snowbird, ICDAR, CIFED, etc. * [A photo and movie gallery of various radio-controled airplanes](http://www.lecun.org/gallery/libhob/index.html), other miniature flying objects, lego robots, and other techno toys. Check out also my [model airplane page](http://www.lecun.org/hobby/planes.html). * [Miscellaneous artsy and nature picture](http://www.lecun.org/gallery/libart/index.html), including garden-variety wild animals, landscapes, etc. * [Vintage airplanes](http://www.lecun.org/gallery/libart/20000816-lebourget/index.html) at the national air and space museum in Le Bourget, near Paris. * No, [Yann is NOT Philippe Kahn's evil brother](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/fun/index.html#kahn.html) * [Your Name can't possibly be pronounced that way](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/fun/index.html#gellman): or how a Nobel prize winner tried to tell me how to pronounce my own name. * [Who is Tex Avery anyway?](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/fun/index.html#tex) * [Steep Learning Curves and other erroneous metaphores](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/fun/index.html#steep) * [Vladimir Vapnik meets the video game sub-culture](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/fun/index.html#allyourbayes) * [Cheap Philosophy (42 cents)](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/fun/index.html#philo) * [A Mathematical Theory of Empty Disclaimers](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/fun/index.html#disclaim) * [The Axis of Rivals](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/fun/index.html#weasel) My former group at AT&T (the Image Processing Research Department) and its ancestor (Larry Jackel's Adaptive Systems Research Department) made numerous contributions to Machine Learning, Image Compression, Pattern Recognition, Synthetic Persons (talking heads), and Neural-Net Hardware. Specific contributions not mentioned elsewhere on this site include the ever so popular Support Vector Machine, the PlayMail and Virt2Elle synthetic talking heads, the Net32K and ANNA neural net chips, and many others. Visit [my former group's home page](http://yann.lecun.com/ex/group/index.html) for more details. Links to interesting places on the web, friends' home pages, etc [.](http://yann.lecun.com/elloww.html)

Meet Figure 02: The AI-Powered Robot Workforce of the Future
============================================================

[![Image 4: Katie Baker](https://em360tech.com/sites/default/files/styles/author_image/public/linkedinImages/user-picture-4489-1706648130914.jpeg.webp?itok=qhaiTWxJ) Katie Baker](https://em360tech.com/user/katie-baker)

Figure 02, the latest humanoid robot from Figure AI, is set to revolutionize the workforce and replace human workers.

This new AI powered robot demonstrated a massive leap forward in robotics, even since the previous iteration, Figure 01, released in 2023.

Figure AI is the company behind the Figure 01 robot, was founded in 2022 by Brett Adcock, the company is dedicated to developing advanced AI-powered humanoid robots.

The $2.6 billion robotics startup, Figure AI, is backed by the likes of Jeff Bezos, [Nvidia](https://em360tech.com/node/29409)and Microsoft. The company has also forged a strategic partnership with [OpenAI](https://em360tech.com/node/29481), which allows them to integrate the Open AI large language models into its robots, enabling more natural and complex interactions.

![Image 5: em360tech image](https://em360tech.com/sites/default/files/styles/cover_image/public/2024-08/figure-02-ai-robot.jpg.webp?itok=PXxlb8Lw)

"Autonomous humanoid workers"
-----------------------------

The goal is to ‘deploy autonomous humanoid workers’ that will support humans on a global scale. The team behind Figure AI aims to address the ‘10 million unfilled jobs’ in the United States, with a particular focus on the approximately 7 million job openings that are in essential warehouses, transportation and retail positions.

As part of his ‘master plan’, founder Brett Adcok says he hopes that the Figure robots will ‘eliminate the need for unsafe and undesirable jobs’ and ultimately allow humans to live ‘happier, more purposeful lives.’

He is confident that these robots that can ‘think, learn, reason, and interact with their environments’ will eventually outperform humans and has hopes that ‘humans could leave the loop’ when these robots become capable of building other robots.

The initial focus is robots built for manufacturing, carrying out ‘structured and repetitive tasks’. However, as the robots continue to advance they will be able to take on more complex job functions, first within the manufacturing and shipping industries before expanding to cover ‘corporate labor roles (3+ billion humans), to assisting individuals in the home (2+ billion)’ and ‘caring for the elderly (~1 billion)’.

The ‘master plan’ makes it clear that Adcock’s focus is for the robots to take on ‘jobs that humans don’t want to perform’ rather than replace human workers.

What’s new with the Figure 02 robot?
------------------------------------

The latest version of FigureAI’s humanoid robot, Figure 02, has increased its computational threefold since its previous model threefold, enabling it to tackle complex tasks autonomously.

Its advanced vision is facilitated by six onboard cameras, paired with an ability to perceive and understand. This heightened understanding is paired with the advanced communication capabilities, supported by OpenAI’s large language models as well as microphones and speakers.

The Figure 02 robot has also undergone significant physical upgrades, including increased hand dexterity with 16 degrees of freedom per hand, allow for precise manipulation of objects. Strength has doubled compared to its predecessor, with the capacity to lift up to 25 kilograms. To support these demanding operations, the battery life has been extended by over 50% to 5 hours.

![Image 6: what-is-figure-02-figureai-humanoid-robot](https://em360tech.com/sites/default/files/inline-images/what-is-figure-02-figureai-humanoid-robot.jpg)
The advanced Figure 02 robot has successfully completed trials at BMW's Spartanburg plant, demonstrating its ability to perform complex tasks with precision and efficiency. By handling repetitive and physically demanding duties, Figure 02 frees up human workers to focus on higher-level tasks, enhancing overall productivity and job satisfaction.

As humanoid robots become increasingly sophisticated, it's important to address ethical implications. Issues such as job displacement, privacy, and the potential misuse of technology need careful consideration.

[Read: What is XAI? Explainable AI Explained](https://em360tech.com/node/29362)

Figure AI emphasises the importance of developing robots that support human capabilities rather than replace them, but balancing economic growth with social responsibility will be crucial.

Davos 2025: A Provocative Claim
-------------------------------

At the World Economic Forum in Davos (January 2025), Meta’s Chief AI Scientist **Yann LeCun** made a statement that reverberated across the technology world:

> _“Nobody in their right mind will use Generative AI and Large Language Models in the next five years.”_

For many, this sounded extreme. After all, LLMs like GPT, Claude, and Gemini are embedded in search engines, productivity tools, coding assistants, and enterprise workflows. But LeCun’s critique was not about dismissing their current usefulness. Instead, it was a challenge: **today’s models are fundamentally flawed, and a paradigm shift is overdue.**

The Four Critical Shortcomings of Today’s LLMs
----------------------------------------------

LeCun outlined four specific deficiencies that prevent LLMs from being the foundation of long-term AI progress:

1.   **No grounding in the physical world.**

 LLMs only manipulate symbols (text) without connecting them to sensory or real-world experiences. They cannot tell whether a sentence about balancing a glass of water on a tilted table makes physical sense.
2.   **Lack of continuous memory.**

 They start fresh each time. Even with retrieval-augmented systems, their memory is external and brittle. Humans, by contrast, accumulate lifelong experiences.
3.   **Weak reasoning abilities.**

 Current models are powerful pattern matchers but stumble with logical inference, causality, or counterfactual thinking.
4.   **Poor long-term planning.**

 They cannot plan multi-step strategies in a dynamic environment. Ask a model to design and execute a multi-day robotics task, and it fails.

These are not minor gaps — they define the boundary between **statistical text prediction** and **true intelligence**.

LeCun’s Alternative: Towards “World Models”
-------------------------------------------

LeCun and Meta’s FAIR (Fundamental AI Research) team are working on what he calls **world models**: AI systems that build an internal simulation of reality. Instead of predicting the next word, these systems would:

*   **Learn physical and causal structure** (e.g., predicting how objects fall, roll, or break).
*   **Develop common-sense reasoning** through simulation, not just text.
*   **Use hierarchical planning** to achieve goals across time, much like humans break down tasks.
*   **Integrate continuous memory** that accumulates knowledge dynamically.

This represents a move away from **Generative Pretrained Transformers (GPT-style models)** towards architectures inspired by robotics, reinforcement learning, and cognitive science.

Industry Examples Beyond Meta
-----------------------------

While Meta is vocal, other labs are also exploring directions that echo LeCun’s critique:

*   **DeepMind’s Gato and Gemini projects**: Aiming for multi-modal models that can handle text, vision, and control signals, not just language. This pushes toward general agents.
*   **OpenAI’s work on agents**: Experiments with memory persistence and planning (e.g., ChatGPT with long-term memory, autonomous code agents).
*   **Anthropic’s Constitutional AI**: While framed around safety, its research points to the need for models that reason transparently and follow higher-order rules, not just word patterns.
*   **Nvidia’s robotics research**: Building embodied AI systems that combine simulation environments (Isaac Gym, Omniverse) with learning, aligning with LeCun’s “decade of robotics.”

These efforts suggest the field is already moving from **pure text generation** toward **grounded, embodied, reasoning-capable systems**.

The Decade of Robotics
----------------------

LeCun predicts that the 2020s will become the “decade of robotics.” This does not mean humanoid robots everywhere, but rather:

*   **AI systems that learn through interaction with the world**, not just static datasets.
*   **Virtual world models** that allow AI to rehearse and refine reasoning before acting in reality.
*   **Robotics as a forcing function** for AI research, since planning, memory, and reasoning are indispensable in embodied environments.

Just as ImageNet drove the deep learning revolution in vision, robotics could be the next benchmark that forces breakthroughs.

Why This Matters
----------------

LeCun’s warning should not be dismissed as contrarian. Instead, it highlights:

*   **LLMs are a transitional technology.** Their fluency masks deeper limitations.
*   **Enterprises must be cautious.** Betting entirely on today’s LLMs may create technical debt when new paradigms emerge.
*   **Investors and policymakers must prepare.** The next five years may bring disruptive shifts — from language-first models to grounded, multimodal world models.

The future of AI will be defined less by bigger datasets and more by **architectures capable of reasoning, memory, and physical understanding**.

Closing Thought
---------------

LeCun’s Davos message is not anti-AI — it is a roadmap. Current LLMs are the floppy disks of artificial intelligence: useful, even transformative, but destined to be replaced by architectures that think, reason, and act with true understanding.

Meet Phoenix Robot of Sanctuary AI and Tesla’s Latest Launch, Optimus!
======================================================================

[![Image 6: K.C. Sabreena Basheer](https://av-eks-lekhak.s3.amazonaws.com/media/lekhak-profile-images/converted_image_GIbx21k.webp)](https://www.analyticsvidhya.com/blog/author/sabreena/)

[K.C. Sabreena Basheer](https://www.analyticsvidhya.com/blog/author/sabreena/) Last Updated : 04 Jun, 2025 

 3 min read 

0

Sanctuary AI, a Vancouver-based company, has introduced its 6th generation robot named Phoenix, which is designed to offer ‘labor-as-a-service’ to tackle labor challenges faced by organizations today. They built this general-purpose robot with advanced AI capabilities, allowing it to integrate seamlessly into the workforce in various industries. The company’s unique ‘labor-as-a-service’ business model allows customers to rent out these robots and pay negotiated rates for their work performed, instead of investing in one themselves. Meanwhile, Tesla has announced their latest venture – Optimus, a humanoid robot that promises to free humans from “dangerous, repetitive, and boring” tasks. They previewed the robot recently, which features advanced sensors and AI capabilities.

![Image 7: Meet the latest robots, Sanctuary AI's Phoenix and Tesla's Optimus. With Advanced AI capabilities these humanoids will make your life easier.](https://cdn.analyticsvidhya.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/phoenix-2.jpeg)

Meet Phoenix, the World’s First Commercially Available General-Purpose Humanoid Robot
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Phoenix is the world’s first humanoid general-purpose robot powered by Carbon™, an advanced [AI](https://www.analyticsvidhya.com/blog/2021/09/introduction-to-artificial-intelligence-for-beginners/) software system designed to give it human-like intelligence. It completed “110 retail-related tasks, including picking and packing merchandise, cleaning, tagging, labeling, folding, and more.” Phoenix features extremely dexterous robotic hands with 20 degrees of freedom of movement. It makes it enable to manipulate objects like a human hand. The hands incorporate proprietary haptic technology that enables the robot to “feel” as humans do.

![Image 8: Specifications of Phoenix, a general purpose robot.](https://cdn.analyticsvidhya.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/sanctuary-phoenix.jpg)
Carbon™: A Revolutionary Cognitive Architecture and Software Platform for Robots
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Carbon™ is a revolutionary cognitive architecture and software platform for general-purpose humanoid robots. It integrates modern AI technologies to translate natural language into action in the real world. Carbon™ enables Phoenix to think and act like a person to complete tasks. The system uses explainable and auditable reasoning, task, and motion plans, symbolic and logical reasoning coupled with modern LLMs for general knowledge, domain-specific integrations and extensions, agency and goal-seeking behaviors, and [Deep Learning](https://www.analyticsvidhya.com/blog/2021/12/a-guide-on-deep-learning-from-basics-to-advanced-concepts/)&[Reinforcement Learning](https://www.analyticsvidhya.com/blog/2021/02/introduction-to-reinforcement-learning-for-beginners/). It also employs photo-realistic and physics-realistic world simulations for robot training and human-in-the-loop supervision, teleoperation, and fleet management.

Tesla Shows Progress on Optimus Bot
-----------------------------------

Tesla, known for its AI-enabled cars, is now working on a humanoid robot, Optimus. They shared the first glance of the bot at the shareholders’ meeting this week.

The Tesla Bot will help humans get free from dangerous, boring, and repetitive tasks. The humanoid stands 5 ft. 8 in. tall, weighs 125 lbs, and can lift objects heavier than itself. The test video shows Optimus picking things up, stacking boxes, and helping with mechanical jobs.

![Image 9: Tesla Bot has the characteristics: world built by humans, for humans, friendly, eliminates dangerous, repetitive, boring tasks, height 5'8, carry capacity 45 LBS, weight 125 LBS, deadlift 150 LBS, speed 5 MPH, arm extend lift 10 LBS](https://cdn.analyticsvidhya.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/tesla-bot.jpg)
Future of Robotics: Incorporating Generalized Real-World AI
-----------------------------------------------------------

Elon Musk, the CEO of Tesla, has been working on developing generalized real-world AI for Tesla’s fully self-driven cars, which could be incorporated into humanoid robots like Optimus. Musk believes that every person would want at least one robot, estimating its demand to be 10 – 20 billion units.

Our Say
-------

Sanctuary AI’s launch of a humanoid robot for rental is a revolutionary step in the field of robotics. As organizations continue to face labor challenges, this technology could help fill gaps in the labor market. With the integration of advanced AI software systems like Carbon™ and the potential incorporation of generalized real-world AI developed by Tesla, we can expect to see even more sophisticated robots in the future.

34.description:
Sanctuary AI today unveiled the seventh generation of its general purpose 
robot Phoenix™. The latest...
34.content:
![Image 1: Introducing Phoenix Gen 7 robot by Sanctuary AI](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/66e8617ff9cbf43e43b040ef/1726505361896-92GLPSBISSECL0819ACV/sanctuaryai_website2.jpg)

*   Generation 7 of ‘Phoenix’ robots include improved human-like range of motion

*   Improvements in uptime, visual perception, and tactile sensing increase the capability of the system to perform complex tasks over longer periods

*   Design iteration significantly decreases build time

*   The speed at which new tasks can be automated has increased 50x, marking a major inflection point in task automation speed

**VANCOUVER, CANADA –**[Sanctuary AI](https://sanctuary.ai/), a company on a mission to create the world’s first human-like intelligence in general purpose robots, today unveiled the seventh generation of its general purpose robot Phoenix™. The latest generation robot and its AI control system, Carbon™, draw even closer to that of a person, with wide ranging improvements to both the hardware and AI software. The announcement comes less than 12 months after Sanctuary AI’s sixth generation robot ([one of TIME’s best inventions of 2023](https://sanctuary.ai/resources/news/sanctuary-ai-named-on-time-s-best-inventions-of-2023-list/)) was launched, and less than 16 months after its fifth generation robot was [first commercially deployed](https://sanctuary.ai/resources/news/sanctuary-ai-deploys-first-humanoid-general-purpose-robot-commercially/) in January 2023.

This generation of Phoenix is one of the most sophisticated human behavioral data capture technologies available today, providing Carbon with some of the highest quality, highest fidelity, training data available. The changes include:

*   Increased uptime, making robots more available for training and data capture

*   Increased build and commissioning speed, allowing us to bring more units online faster

*   Reduced bill of materials, lowering the cost of manufacture

*   Significant hardware improvements, increasing range of motion in the wrists, hands, and elbows, and increasing hand durability

*   Further miniaturized hydraulics, reducing the weight, power consumption, and complexity with increased hardware and software measures that exceed specified safety standards

*   Improved visual acuity and tactile sensing, leading to higher-fidelity data to train the AI control system

*   The time it takes for new tasks to be automated has gone from weeks to less than 24 hours, marking a major inflection point in task automation speed and autonomous system capability

“It’s incredible to see the progress that has been made in just 11 months,” said Geordie Rose, former CEO and Co-Founder of Sanctuary AI. “With Generation 7, we have a system that we believe is the most closely analogous to a person of any available. We see this as not only the cornerstone of general purpose AI robotics but a critical step on the path to artificial general intelligence, and we’re thrilled to be leading the charge on it. This all adds up to being able to capture increasing quantities of higher quality, higher fidelity human behavioral data, which in turn will expedite the development of foundational AI models and customer deployments.”

**About Sanctuary AI**

Founded in 2018, [Sanctuary AI](https://sanctuary.ai/) is a multi-award-winning company based in Vancouver, Canada. Sanctuary AI is on a mission to create the world's first human-like intelligence in general purpose robots that will help us work more safely, efficiently, and sustainably, helping to address the labor challenges facing many organizations today. Sanctuary AI's growing list of customers and investors represents a wide variety of industries across Canada, the US, and other countries around the world.

Members of the Sanctuary AI team founded D-Wave (a pioneer in the quantum computing industry), Kindred (first use of reinforcement learning in a production robot), and the Creative Destruction Lab (pioneered a revolutionary method for the commercialization of science for the betterment of humankind). With experience at startups and technology leaders such as Amazon, Microsoft, and Softbank Robotics, the team has experience launching market-defining innovations rooted in previously unsolved and deep scientific problems.

It has torque sensor feedback in all joints, enabling dynamic balancing and multi-contact motions. * **AI and Software:** The robot runs on ROS (Robot Operating System) and uses Ubuntu Linux OS, with real-time control loops and simulation capabilities through Gazebo. * **Applications:** TALOS is primarily used in industrial settings for tasks like drilling and screwing, and in research environments for developing advanced human-robot interaction skills. * **Sensors and Actuators:** Equipped with RGB-D cameras, inertial measurement units (IMUs), and force/torque sensors on each foot and wrist, TALOS can sense its environment accurately and interact with objects precisely. ### **Technical Specifications:** * **Height:** 175 cm * **Weight:** 95 kg * **Payload Capacity:** 6 kg per arm when fully extended * **Speed:** Up to 3 km/h * **Sensors:** Torque sensors in all joints, RGB-D camera, IMU * **Actuators:** 32 high-torque brushless DC motors * **Degrees of Freedom:** 32 DoF (Leg: 6 DoF x 2; Arm: 7 DoF x 2; Gripper: 1 DoF x 2; Waist: 2 DoF; Neck: 2 DoF) * **Compute:** Two Intel Core i7 CPUs * **Power:** 1080-Wh lithium-ion battery, providing 1.5 hours of walking operation and 3 hours on standby.](https://www.tophumanoidrobots.com/items/talos/)

Her development has sparked discussions on AI ethics and the future of robotics, serving as a symbol of how AI can integrate into various aspects of human life. ### **Key Features:** * **Design and Appearance:** Sophia's face is made of patented "Frubber" (flesh rubber), a material that mimics human skin and allows her to display over 60 facial expressions. Her design is inspired by Audrey Hepburn and Amanda Hanson, the wife of David Hanson, the founder of Hanson Robotics. * **AI Capabilities:** Sophia uses advanced AI techniques such as face tracking, emotion recognition, and deep neural networks to simulate human-like behavior. She can recognize faces, understand speech, and engage in conversations using natural language processing. * **Applications:** Sophia is designed for research, education, and entertainment. She has been used in various roles, including customer service, event hosting, and promoting products. * **Recognition:** Sophia gained international recognition when she was granted honorary citizenship by Saudi Arabia in 2017, becoming the world's first robot citizen. She is also the first robot Innovation Ambassador for the United Nations Development Programme. ### **Technical Specifications:** * **Height:** 167 cm (5 feet 6 inches) * **Weight:** 20 kg (44 pounds) * **Sensors:** Includes Intel RealSense camera, custom 720p HD cameras for eyes, and audio localization array. * **Actuators:** Uses Dynamixel and Xpert servos for facial and arm movements. * **Degrees of Freedom:** 83 degrees of freedom for enhanced mobility and expression](https://www.tophumanoidrobots.com/items/sophia/)

It stands at approximately 5 feet 7 inches (1.7 meters) tall and weighs around 155 pounds (70 kg in some models), with a payload capacity of up to 55 pounds (25 kg in earlier models). It has been designed with both bipedal and wheeled configurations to enhance stability and functionality. * **AI Integration:** The Carbon AI system provides Phoenix with human-like intelligence, enabling it to learn new tasks quickly and adapt to real-world conditions. It combines symbolic and neural reasoning with deep learning and reinforcement learning for enhanced decision-making. * **Applications:** Phoenix excels in healthcare by assisting with patient care, in manufacturing by performing assembly tasks, and in retail by handling customer service roles. * **Safety Features:** Equipped with advanced sensors and navigation systems, Phoenix ensures safe interaction with humans and its environment, avoiding obstacles autonomously. ### **Technical Specifications:** * **Height:** 5 feet 7 inches (1.7 meters) * **Weight:** 155 pounds (70 kg in some models) * **Payload Capacity:** Up to 55 pounds (25 kg in earlier models) * **Max Speed:** Approximately 3 miles per hour * **AI System:** Carbon AI for human-like intelligence and adaptability](https://www.tophumanoidrobots.com/items/phoenix/)

37.title: Digit's Next Steps
37.content:
At Agility Robotics, we're building robots that are made for work. As our robot Digit enters more job sites, we must have a state-of-the-art navigation stack that’s focused on real-world deployments and creating value for our customers.

We recently celebrated the one-year anniversary of Digit's full-time deployment at GXO. In this bustling facility, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) arrive at Digit's station carrying totes of product from the order picking area. Digit efficiently unloads these AMRs and loads the totes onto a conveyor, sending them to pack-out stations. To be efficient in dynamic warehouse facilities like this one, robots face a number of challenges. They must navigate tightly constrained spaces, carry heavy objects, and frequently stop and turn in place to successfully handle materials.

Optimizing To Meet Customer Requirements
----------------------------------------

To increase Digit’s efficiency on the job, our navigation team completely redesigned the robot’s navigation stack. The robot now solves for the globally optimal, minimum-step path to the goal. This footstep path is then precisely tracked by a sophisticated model-predictive controller, ensuring Digit makes no unnecessary movements. This improved approach has several benefits for the robot:

*   **Tightened Movement**-Fewer steps when transitioning to standing, or during tight turns.
*   **Improved Performance with a Payload**- Digit accounts for carrying heavy objects and navigates with them at greater speeds.
*   **Ease in Confined Spaces**-Digit maneuvers dependably in tight environments, even while carrying bulky objects.

Your browser does not support the video tag.

Real-World Impact: Upgrades in Action
-------------------------------------

One impressive demonstration of Digit's adaptability is its ability to handle workflow fluctuations. When downstream stations are backed up or employees are on a break, Digit intelligently stacks totes to the side instead of placing them directly on the conveyor. This ensures the flow of AMRs through the facility continues uninterrupted. Once the conveyor is clear, Digit seamlessly loads the queued-up totes and switches back to its primary task of unloading arriving AMRs.

The improvements to Digit's navigation capabilities directly translate to faster cycle times in these critical workflows, leading to higher throughput and greater value for our customers**.**

36.title: Digit Moves Over 100,000 Totes in Commercial Deployment
36.content:
As those who have worked within logistics facilities know, the proof is in the throughput. To achieve necessary throughput and tackle persistent labor shortages, logistics leaders must find ways to scale operations efficiently and redeploy human talent to higher-value tasks, away from monotonous or repetitive work cycles. New automation technologies are crucial for this transformation. But if that new automation can’t maintain performance across thousands of cycles and handle varying conditions over an extended deployment, it’s a liability, not an asset.

For us here at Agility Robotics, we’ve always dedicated ourselves to moving past the novelty of humanoids and focused on providing an essential operational tool and solution for our customers. Today we celebrate a crucial milestone as Digit, our general-purpose humanoid, has moved over 100,000 totes at GXO’s Flowery Branch facility. True industrial validation requires proving a robot's capacity for high-volume, reliable throughput, effectively establishing a clear, long-term Return on Investment (ROI) and proves that the automation can be scaled successfully across the enterprise. Having a true general-purpose humanoid is the linchpin, but what does that look like and how did we get there?

Deploying Humanoids in Modern Logistics Facilities
--------------------------------------------------

We often hear the term "general-purpose humanoid," but what does this new category of robot actually mean, and how does it differ from today's automation? A general-purpose humanoid is defined by its human form factor- two legs, two arms, and a torso- which is designed for versatility and adaptability. This form allows the robots to operate within human-centric environments, using the same tools and infrastructure without extensive retrofitting. This capability is what truly separates it from existing robots like fixed robotic arms or autonomous mobile robots (AMRs). While AMRs and robotic arms are highly effective at a single, specialized task like transporting goods or machine tending, humanoids like Digit can perform a wide variety of unrelated tasks within the same workflow. Digit's work has demonstrated this evolution, not only picking items on and off an AMR to a conveyor, but also stacking totes onto a different floor location, proving its capacity for multi-tasking and real-world generalization.

Your browser does not support the video tag.

Being able to do these types of tasks reliably and consistently with high weight payload capabilities validates the Agility solution's role as a transformative asset, poised to deliver immediate and sustained productivity gains for our customers.

Translating AI Hype into Tangible Applications in Logistics
-----------------------------------------------------------

“AI”, the defining buzzword of the decade. But how does this technology translate from science fiction “buzzword” to valuable and practical applications with today's humanoid robots? Digit is at the forefront of putting AI to work in the real world, and we’re taking a measured, reliable approach to deploying learned methods at scale. Our learning from demonstration pipeline blends traditional control methods, teleoperated demonstrations, policy training, and refinement through reinforcement learning and simulation to deliver new skills and validated behaviors that provide real-world value on customer sites. Real world deployments in dynamic environments are crucial for validating and hardening Digit's core capabilities such as:

*   Dynamic Balancing: Maintaining stability while walking and carrying payloads of varying weights.
*   Vision Accuracy: Reliably identifying and grasping objects thousands of times under different lighting conditions and placement configurations.

Reaching the 100K milestone demonstrates our system's capacity for seamless and consistent integration into existing operational workflows (not just single, isolated behaviors) and proprietary systems at major logistics facilities.

Your browser does not support the video tag.

Setting the Safety Standard
---------------------------

For Third-Party Logistics (3PLs), safety is not merely a compliance check- it’s the financial gatekeeper to all automation investment. Simply put: there is no scale without safety. By deploying Digit long-term in live production environments, Agility is actively proving the viability of safe human-robot teaming.

Agility is dedicated to forging the path for a cooperatively safe humanoid workforce. This commitment builds the operational trust and regulatory confidence required for 3PLs to successfully integrate and scale humanoid technology and unlock the full value of humanoid automation.

A Shared Vision
---------------

This milestone is a shared success, proving what’s possible when technological innovation and operational leadership converge. This achievement requires more than just an advanced robotics solution, it requires a partner like GXO who possesses both a long-term vision for automation and the expertise to integrate it into a live fulfillment environment.

Together, we are building the blueprint for safe, effective, and scalable human-robot collaboration in logistics.

‍

To learn more about our humanoid solution, please [visit our solution page.](https://www.agilityrobotics.com/solution)

40.title: Best Humanoid Robots Available in 2025 | Robozaps
40.description: Explore our guide to find the best humanoid robots for 2025, transforming industries and daily lives. Find the best models available at Robozaps.
40.content:
Humanoid robots have transitioned from futuristic fantasies to indispensable tools, transforming industries and redefining human-robot partnerships. Today’s top humanoid robots blend cutting-edge artificial intelligence, remarkable agility, and lifelike functionality to address diverse challenges, from factory automation to personal support. In this section, we explore nine exceptional humanoid robots shaping 2025: Figure 02, DIGIT, AMECA, Optimus, Walker S, Apollo, Phoenix, AgiBot A2, and Unitree G1. Here’s a deep dive into what sets each apart.

The Best Humanoid Robots of 2025
--------------------------------

Humanoid robots in 2025 are breaking barriers in affordability, versatility, and advanced functionality. Below is a detailed look at the year’s standout robots, their innovations, and their applications.

### Figure 02 by Figure AI

![Image 1: A robot with sleek, gray body and a black head, is positioned in front of a stark white background, its right hand open and slightly raised](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67ea6793adf74f7d3087e4e4/67f5303640ff1978a92f103e_Figure_02_robo_fabricas_1%20(1).avif)

 Best Humanoid Robots: Figure 02 by Figure AI

**Key Features:**Figure 02 boasts high-torque motors (up to 150Nm) and human-like hands with 24 degrees of freedom, delivering unmatched precision and dexterity.

**Applications:** This robot shines in manufacturing and logistics, performing tasks like assembly, material handling, and intricate repairs alongside human workers.

**Availability:**Commercially available, Figure 02 is already deployed in select industrial environments, with wider rollout anticipated soon.

‍

### DIGIT by Agility Robotics

![Image 2: Two teal and white robots, one of which is holding a grey bin on a blue metal shelf](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67ea6793adf74f7d3087e4e4/67f530909375fbb943ceb207_agility-robotics-digit.avif)

Digit by Agility Robotics

**Key Features:**Designed for endurance, DIGIT can operate for an 8-hour shift on one charge. Its adaptive grippers and AI-driven navigation enable it to handle diverse objects and environments.

**Applications:** A top choice for warehouses, DIGIT excels at picking, packing, and transporting goods, making it one of the best humanoid robots for logistics.

**Availability:**Available for purchase, DIGIT is currently in use in several warehouse settings, with plans for broader logistics adoption.

### Tesla Optimus

![Image 3: A Tesla robot in a black and white color scheme](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67ea6793adf74f7d3087e4e4/67f530ebf5301ed5bb427cdb_5-2.avif)

Tesla Optimus

**Key Features:** Optimus combines versatility and advanced AI, with a sleek design and improved hands tailored for diverse tasks.

**Applications:** Set to debut in Tesla factories for tasks like assembly and maintenance, it also holds potential for future home assistance roles, such as cleaning or caregiving.

**Availability:**Still in development, Optimus is slated for limited production in 2025, starting with Tesla’s own facilities.

### Unitree G1

![Image 4: A humanoid robot is standing with black gloves and black shoes](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67ea6793adf74f7d3087e4e4/67f5331cde996c54734546a7_unitree-g1.avif)

Unitree G1

**Highlights:**Compact yet capable, Unitree G1 offers 23 degrees of freedom, 3D LiDAR, and depth cameras for sharp environmental awareness.

**Uses:** Popular in research and education, it also suits light industrial duties and elderly care applications.

**Status:**Available for purchase, it’s a go-to choice for academics and developers diving into humanoid robotics.

### AgiBot A2

![Image 5: The humanoid AgiBot robot is seen from the torso up](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67ea6793adf74f7d3087e4e4/67ebad9754fe7c0e2efc8b69_a2-l2-1.webp)

AgiBot A2

**Highlights:**Tailored for service, AgiBot A2 features an ergonomic design, AI-powered sensors, and human-like interaction skills, excelling in precision tasks like threading a needle.

**Uses:**Perfect for customer service, marketing, and exhibitions, it boosts engagement in public-facing environments.

**Status:**Available for service-focused industries, it’s gaining popularity where human-like interaction is key.

### Walker S by UBTECH

![Image 6: The robot stands in a room with white walls, facing the viewer](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67ea6793adf74f7d3087e4e4/67f534a84c1524ef8cba2743_ubtech-walker-s%201.avif)

UBTECH Walker S

**Highlights:** With 41 servo joints, advanced sensors, and large language model integration, Walker S provides precise movement and responsive feedback.

**Uses:** A manufacturing favorite, it conducts quality checks and supports assembly lines, ranking among the top humanoid robots for industrial accuracy.

**Status:**Commercially available, it’s already enhancing operations in facilities like Audi’s China plant.

‍

### Apollo by Apptronik

![Image 7: The robot is standing, with the head having two holes where eyes should be, in front of a white background](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67ea6793adf74f7d3087e4e4/67f53550f0d5a9c55b832c13_apollo-robot.avif)

Apptronik Apollo

**Highlights:** Apollo boasts a 55-lb payload capacity, a customizable modular design, and safety features like LED displays and force control for smooth human collaboration.

**Uses:** Suited for warehouses, manufacturing, and construction, it handles heavy lifting and repetitive jobs with ease.

**Status:**Available to industrial buyers, Apollo is active in logistics and production hubs.

‍

### NEO (1X Robotics)

![Image 8: NEO (1X Robotics)](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67ea6793adf74f7d3087e4e4/67efc9f0c9ea657fc127592d_NEO-1X-Robotics-1024x558.jpeg)

NEO is designed to serve as a personal companion and assistant, tailored for individuals seeking home-based support. It emphasizes human-centric design and intuitive interaction, making it ideal for caregiving roles, including assisting the elderly or disabled. NEO also aims to integrate into smart home ecosystems, acting as a central hub for managing connected devices and enhancing daily living experiences.

**Features:**

*   Human-centric design for natural interactions.
*   AI-driven adaptability for user-specific needs.
*   Compact and elegant build to blend into home environments.

**Use Cases:**

*   Assisting individuals with disabilities or elderly care.
*   Smart home integration and management.
*   Personal assistant for everyday tasks.

These robots represent the forefront of humanoid robotics, blending affordability with groundbreaking innovation to address diverse needs across industries and homes.

‍

Comparative Analysis
--------------------

### How Do These Robots Compare?

With so many top humanoid robots available in 2025, choosing the right one depends on understanding their unique strengths and specifications. Below, we’ve created a comparison table that highlights key differences in height, weight, payload capacity, battery life, and primary applications. This side-by-side view makes it easy to see which robot excels in areas like industrial strength, endurance, or human interaction.

Best Humanoid Robots Comparison

| Robot | Height | Weight | Payload | Battery Life | Key Applications |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Figure 02** | 5'6" (168 cm) | 150 lbs (68 kg) | 44 lbs (20 kg) | 6 hours | Manufacturing, Logistics |
| **DIGIT** | 5'9" (175 cm) | 140 lbs (64 kg) | 35 lbs (16 kg) | 8 hours | Warehouses |
| **AMECA** | 5'7" (170 cm) | 120 lbs (54 kg) | N/A | 4 hours | Human Interaction |
| **Optimus** | 5'8" (173 cm) | 160 lbs (73 kg) | 45 lbs (20 kg) | TBD | Industrial, Domestic |
| **Walker S** | 5'5" (165 cm) | 130 lbs (59 kg) | 33 lbs (15 kg) | 6 hours | Manufacturing |
| **Apollo** | 6'0" (183 cm) | 180 lbs (82 kg) | 55 lbs (25 kg) | 7 hours | Warehouses |
| **Phoenix** | 5'6" (168 cm) | 135 lbs (61 kg) | 30 lbs oper(14 kg) | 5 hours | Retail, Service |
| **AgiBot A2** | 5'9" (175 cm) | 121 lbs (55 kg) | 22 lbs (10 kg) | 5 hours | Customer Service |
| **Unitree G1** | 4'2" (127 cm) | 77 lbs (35 kg) | 17.6 lbs (8 kg) | 2 hours | Research, Education |

### Key Insights from the Comparison

Apollo stands out with the highest payload capacity at 55 lbs (25 kg), making it the powerhouse for heavy lifting in warehouses and manufacturing.

DIGIT leads in endurance, offering an impressive 8-hour battery life, perfect for long shifts in logistics without frequent recharging.

AMECA, while not designed for physical tasks, is unmatched in human interaction, thanks to its advanced AI and expressive capabilities.

Optimus and Walker S provide balanced performance for industrial settings, with Optimus also showing potential for future domestic use.

Phoenix and AgiBot A2 excel in service-oriented roles, with Phoenix specializing in retail tasks and AgiBot A2 in customer engagement.

Unitree G1, the most compact robot on the list, offers flexibility and affordability, making it ideal for research and educational environments.

**Takeaway:** The best humanoid robot for you depends on your specific needs. For raw power and heavy-duty tasks, Apollo or Figure 02 are top contenders. For endurance in logistics, DIGIT is the clear choice. If human interaction is key, AMECA or AgiBot A2 are unmatched. And for research or educational purposes, Unitree G1 offers a versatile, budget-friendly option.

Market Trends and Future Outlook
--------------------------------

### The Future of Humanoid Robots

The humanoid robotics market is on the cusp of a major transformation, driven by technological innovation and a growing need for automation. In 2024, the market was valued at $2.03 billion, with projections estimating it will climb to over $13 billion by 2029. This explosive growth highlights the expanding role of humanoid robots in industries and everyday life. As we head into 2025, several trends are shaping the trajectory of the best humanoid robots, setting the stage for a future where these machines are more integrated into our world than ever before.

### Rapid Market Growth and Adoption

The dramatic rise in market value reflects increasing demand for humanoid robots across diverse sectors, including manufacturing, logistics, retail, and personal assistance. Businesses are adopting these robots to tackle labor shortages, boost efficiency, and cut costs. For example, robots like DIGIT and Apollo are revolutionizing warehouse operations, while Phoenix is proving its worth in retail by managing tasks like inventory restocking. Experts predict that by 2026, humanoid robots could become a common sight in workplaces, mirroring their current prevalence in industrial settings.

### Key Trends Driving the Industry

**Several forces are propelling the humanoid robotics market forward:**

**Advanced AI Integration:**Today’s best humanoid robots are smarter and more adaptable, thanks to breakthroughs in artificial intelligence. Models like AMECA and Optimus use advanced AI, including large language models, to interact naturally with humans and perform complex tasks with greater precision.

**Affordability and Accessibility:** As production costs decline, humanoid robots are becoming more attainable. Robots like Unitree G1 offer cost-effective solutions for education and research, while industrial options like Walker S are now viable for smaller businesses. This trend is broadening the reach of robotics, paving the way for widespread adoption.

**Human-Robot Collaboration:**Far from replacing humans, many humanoid robots are designed to work alongside them. Robots like Figure 02 and AgiBot A2 enhance productivity in factories and service roles, reducing physical strain on workers and fostering a collaborative approach to automation.

### Challenges and Considerations

**While the outlook is promising, the industry faces significant challenges:**

**Technical Limitations:** Key areas like battery life, dexterity, and mobility still need improvement. For instance, DIGIT offers an impressive 8-hour battery life, but many robots require frequent recharging, limiting their practicality for long shifts.

**Regulatory and Ethical Concerns:** As humanoid robots become more common, issues like data privacy, safety standards, and ethical implications—particularly in human-facing roles—come to the forefront. Developers and regulators are working to address these concerns, but solutions remain a work in progress.

**The Road Ahead:**Humanoid Robots in Everyday Life

Looking forward, humanoid robots are set to expand beyond industrial applications into homes, healthcare, and more. By 2026, robots like Optimus could be assisting with household tasks, while others might offer companionship or support for aging populations. Researchers are pushing the boundaries of intelligence and adaptability, with some forecasting that by 2040, billions of humanoid robots could be part of daily life.

The best humanoid robots of today are just a glimpse of what’s to come. With AI advancements and falling costs, the next wave of robots will be more affordable, capable, and human-like, offering exciting possibilities for businesses and individuals alike. Keeping an eye on these developments will be essential to unlocking the full potential of humanoid robotics in the years ahead.

Choosing the Right Humanoid Robot
---------------------------------

### Which Humanoid Robot is Best for You?

Selecting the right humanoid robot from the best available today depends on your specific goals, budget, and operational needs. With a variety of options excelling in different areas—ranging from industrial automation to human interaction—it’s essential to evaluate key factors before making a decision. Below, we break down the considerations and offer tailored recommendations to help you choose the perfect robot for your use case.

### Key Factors to Consider

**Cost:** Humanoid robots can range from tens of thousands to millions of dollars. For budget-conscious buyers, Unitree G1 offers an affordable entry point for research or education, while industrial robots like Apollo or DIGIT require a higher investment but deliver long-term value through efficiency gains.

**Deployment Timeline:** Some robots, like Figure 02 and Walker S, are ready for immediate commercial use, while others, such as Optimus, are still in development with limited availability. If you need a robot quickly, opt for models already in production.

**Customization and Scalability:** Robots like Apollo and Phoenix offer modular designs, allowing you to tailor their capabilities to specific tasks. This flexibility is ideal for businesses looking to scale or adapt their automation solutions over time.

**Technical Support and Training:** Consider the level of support provided by the manufacturer. Robots like AMECA and AgiBot A2 come with extensive training for human interaction roles, while industrial robots may require specialized technical expertise for integration.

Recommendations Based on Use Case
---------------------------------

**Industrial Automation:** If you need a robot for heavy-duty tasks like assembly or material handling, Apollo or Figure 02 are top choices. Their high payload capacities and durability make them ideal for demanding environments.

**Logistics and Warehousing:** For warehouse operations, DIGIT stands out with its 8-hour battery life and adaptive grippers, ensuring it can handle long shifts without interruption.

**Customer Service and Human Interaction:** AMECA and AgiBot A2 are unmatched in roles requiring social intelligence. Their lifelike expressions and natural language processing make them perfect for enhancing customer experiences.

**Retail and Service:** If you’re looking to automate tasks like stocking shelves or managing inventory, Phoenix offers the dexterity and adaptability needed for delicate, repetitive work.

**Research and Education:** For academic or developmental purposes, Unitree G1 provides a compact, affordable platform with advanced sensors, making it a versatile tool for exploration and innovation.

**Takeaway:**The best humanoid robot for your needs hinges on aligning the robot’s strengths with your operational goals. By evaluating cost, deployment readiness, and customization options, you can make an informed choice that maximizes both efficiency and value.

Conclusion
----------

### The Impact of Humanoid Robots

The best humanoid robots of 2025—Figure 02, DIGIT, AMECA, Optimus, Walker S, Apollo, Phoenix, AgiBot A2, and Unitree G1—are not just technological marvels; they are catalysts for change across industries and daily life. From tackling labor shortages in manufacturing to enhancing customer service with lifelike interactions, these robots are redefining what’s possible. Their ability to work alongside humans, adapt to complex tasks, and continuously learn makes them invaluable assets in a world increasingly reliant on automation.

As the humanoid robotics market surges toward a projected $13 billion by 2029, the impact of these machines will only grow. Whether in factories, warehouses, retail spaces, or homes, humanoid robots are poised to become integral to our future. Staying informed about their advancements and understanding their potential will be key to leveraging their benefits in the years ahead.

41.title: Next-Generation Supply Chain Automation System | Symbotic
41.description: The Symbotic System delivers unmatched efficiency, accuracy & agility, reduces costs, & enables retailers to distribute products to supply chain on-demand.
41.content:

*   [Contact](https://www.symbotic.com/contact/)

[](https://www.symbotic.com/ "Home")
*   [Investors](https://ir.symbotic.com/)
*   [Contact](https://www.symbotic.com/contact/)

SYSTEM BENEFITS
---------------

The Symbotic System delivers unmatched efficiency, accuracy and agility while reducing costs. The flexibility to push inventory to stores, as well as pull inventory through the supply chain on-demand, is a powerful competitive advantage for Symbotic clients.

![Image 1: A businessman in a blue suit holding a tablet in a warehouse with product icons showing shipping, airplane, secure, and settings](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/shutterstock_1160635549-768x432.jpg)

EXPANDING THE BOUNDARIES OF POSSIBLE
------------------------------------

Solutions for a **Complex Supply Chain**
----------------------------------------

Supply chain leaders are challenged by limited labor availability, increasing operating costs, out-of-stocks, SKU proliferation and misalignment of inventory with demand. Traditional warehouse automation doesn’t fully address the challenges. As the backbone of commerce Symbotic transforms the flow of goods and the economics of the supply chain for its customers. The revolutionary A.I.-powered robotic automation platform is designed for the increased need for efficiency, speed and flexibility.

#### Flexibility

Imagine if you could store a limitless number of SKUs in your existing warehouse.

#### Speed

Imagine if a single person could load a trailer in minutes instead of hours.

#### Efficiency

Imagine if you could process the same order volume in 30-60% less space.

TRANSFORMING THE SUPPLY CHAIN
-----------------------------

The Power to

**Transform the Supply Chain**
--------------------------------------------

Modernizing the warehouse allows consumers to get what they need faster and creates benefits for everyone including workers, stores, customers and their local communities.

[![Image 2](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Supply-Chain31.svg)](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Supply-Chain31.svg)

### **Supply Chain**

The flexibility to pull inventory through the supply on-demand is a powerful competitive advantage for Symbotic clients. Products flow through the supply chain seamlessly as both inbound and outbound shipments are quickly processed. The high-density mixed-SKU pallets eliminate wasted space and reduce transportation costs.

[![Image 3](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Warehouse41.svg)](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Warehouse41.svg)

### **Warehouse**

The warehouse becomes a strategic asset through dramatically lower operating costs, increased efficiency and faster inventory turns. The Symbotic System offers increased capacity, flexibility and accuracy combined with reduced stockouts. Warehouse workers acquire new technology skills and benefit from safer and less physically demanding working conditions.

[![Image 4](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Transportation47.svg)](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Transportation47.svg)

### **Transportation**

Fewer trucks are required with ultra-tall, highly stable pallets that maximize the cube of the trailer, resulting in transportation savings. Trucks can be loaded and unloaded in minutes by a single worker, reducing the amount of time a trailer is tied up and freeing up dock doors for more efficient yard management.

[![Image 5](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Stores15.svg)](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Stores15.svg)

### **Store**

Aisle-ready pallets delivered to stores means workers don’t waste time sorting products in the backroom. They can move products directly from the truck to the selling floor – eliminating wasted travel between departments and reducing the time it takes to restock shelves and reducing stockouts. This means store associates can spend more time helping customers and less time on non-value-add tasks.

[![Image 6](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Customer-Delivery71.svg)](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Customer-Delivery71.svg)

### Customer Delivery

Smart pallets built to route-stop sequence allow for more efficient and accurate delivery to customers. Multiple verifiable checkpoints in the system ensure 99.9999% accuracy, resulting in fewer mispicks and higher customer satisfaction. Highly dense and stable pallets reduce damage in the warehouse and enroute to the customer.

[![Image 7](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Consumers22.svg)](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Consumers22.svg)

### **Consumer**

When shelves are quickly stocked and replenished with the right items at the right time, consumers can find the products they need when they need them. This increases customer satisfaction and reduces frustration caused by out-of-stock inventory. The in-store shopping experience is improved by having fewer workers in aisles stocking shelves.

POWERFUL RETURN ON INVESTMENT
-----------------------------

**Fast, Flexible and Efficient**

 Supply Chain Automation
----------------------------------------------------------

The Symbotic System is modular and scalable depending on the needs of the business. A typical implementation results in several tangible benefits for customers.

DRAMATICALLY LOWER OPERATING COST

5-9X OUTBOUND EFFICIENCY IMPROVEMENT

30-60% FOOTPRINT REDUCTION

99.9999% 

TASK ACCURACY

EXCEPTIONAL SKU AGILITY

INCREASED CAPACITY

LOWER TRANSPORTATION COSTS

FASTER INVENTORY TURNS & FEWER STOCKOUTS

REIMAGINE THE SUPPLY CHAIN
--------------------------

Revolutionary **Automation System**
-----------------------------------

Moving Cases Has

 Never Been Easier
------------------------------------

The Symbotic System turns the warehouse into a strategic asset – increasing capacity, speed, and assortment while reducing the costs associated with inventory carrying, transportation, capital expense, product damage, labor, and related injuries.

![Image 8: A 50x41 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/themes/symbotic/library/dist/images//icon-quote.png)

DELIVERING BUSINESS RESULTS

> “Using high-speed robotics and intelligent software to organize and optimize inventory, the Symbotic System helps us get products to our customers quickly and seamlessly by revolutionizing how we receive and distribute products to stores.”

![Image 9](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/walmart-logo-quote-100x100.png~100x100,https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/walmart-logo-quote.png~120x120)

David Guggina Executive Vice President, Supply Chain Operations, Walmart U.S.

[READ MORE](https://corporate.walmart.com/newsroom/2021/07/14/chain-reaction-were-partnering-with-symbotic-to-bring-high-tech-automation-to-our-supply-chain)

SUPPLY CHAIN INNOVATION

A.I.-Powered Robotic Warehouse Automation
-----------------------------------------

![Image 10](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/A001_C004_0809RI-Edited-Symbot.jpg_700x396-100x57.jpg~100x57,https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/A001_C004_0809RI-Edited-Symbot.jpg_700x396-414x234.jpg~414x234,https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/A001_C004_0809RI-Edited-Symbot.jpg_700x396.jpg~700x396)

#### A.I.-powered software seamlessly orchestrates hundreds of autonomous robots.

Autonomous robots with advanced vision and sensing capabilities work together to build optimized mixed-case pallets with relentless efficiency and industry-leading speed. The robots are equipped with a powerful neural processor and traction control that enables unprecedented speed and precision in maneuvering. A proprietary routing algorithm enables the bots, moving at up to 20+ mph, to do this with unmatched efficiency.

![Image 11: robotic-warehouse-automation-storage-bufffering-structure-symbotic](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Dronegenuity-5300-Kettering-Rd.-Brooksville-FL-34602-26.00_00_06_10.Still001-100x56.jpg~100x56,https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Dronegenuity-5300-Kettering-Rd.-Brooksville-FL-34602-26.00_00_06_10.Still001-414x233.jpg~414x233,https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Dronegenuity-5300-Kettering-Rd.-Brooksville-FL-34602-26.00_00_06_10.Still001-768x432.jpg~768x432,https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Dronegenuity-5300-Kettering-Rd.-Brooksville-FL-34602-26.00_00_06_10.Still001-960x540.jpg~960x540,https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Dronegenuity-5300-Kettering-Rd.-Brooksville-FL-34602-26.00_00_06_10.Still001-1440x810.jpg~1440x810,https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Dronegenuity-5300-Kettering-Rd.-Brooksville-FL-34602-26.00_00_06_10.Still001-2440x1373.jpg~2440x1373)

#### A distributed storage and buffering structure maximizes inventory flexibility.

A first-of-its-kind storage structure and distributed storage algorithm maximizes flexibility and enables the highest inventory density in the market. The system can handle virtually any case – from the smallest to the largest, regardless of packaging. It achieves 99.9999% task accuracy via several computer vision systems that digitize each case entering and validate each case picked from the system.

![Image 12: symbotic-system-wide-view-robotic-warehouse-automation](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Symbotic-FL-700x396-1-100x57.jpg~100x57,https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Symbotic-FL-700x396-1-414x234.jpg~414x234,https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Symbotic-FL-700x396-1.jpg~700x396)

#### The Symbotic System is implemented in modules like Lego building blocks.

The modular system is customizable based on the needs of your business, including case volume, order profiles, and product characteristics.Modules and cells can be added seamlessly. This makes the System easily scalable. And because the System takes up significantly less space than traditional material handling systems, additional space is freed up for expansion as the business grows.

BEYOND THE WAREHOUSE
--------------------

Symbotic Unveils Next-Generation Storage for its Warehouse Automation System – Enabling Significantly Reduced Customer Footprint and Faster Case Handling
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 9: Large warehouse interior shot shows endless racks of cardboard boxes, with a cage-like structure enclosing the shelves and contents](https://www.symbotic.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/9_NextGen_Install_Start.1117-768x432.jpg)

**Wilmington, Massachusetts (August 5, 2025)**— [Symbotic Inc.](https://www.symbotic.com/) (Nasdaq: [SYM](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/sym)), a leader in A.I.-enabled robotics technology for the supply chain, today announced the commercial availability of its innovative next-generation storage technology. Designed to significantly enhance the performance of its industry-leading warehouse automation system, the new structure is engineered to deliver substantially increased storage capacity for products, faster deployment and case handling, enhanced fire suppression, and improved seismic adaptability. _To see Symbotic’s next-generation storage, click_[_here_](https://vimeo.com/1105280880/967db461f9?ts=0&share=copy)_._

Symbotic has coupled the exceptional, industry-leading density offered by its current system with a breakthrough innovation that can reduce customers’ storage footprint by up to 40% of its original size. This will enable customers to fit considerably more products into a fixed space, or attain a target storage volume in a smaller footprint. Case handling speed will also be enhanced: the increased storage density will mean shorter – and faster – bot trips per case delivery.

Additionally, Symbotic’s next-generation storage is engineered for rapid deployment. The innovative structure features pre-assembled, precision-manufactured sub-components that will reduce the number of on-site assembly parts by over 90% and lower system implementation time at customer sites.

Further key benefits of Symbotic’s next-generation storage design include:

*   **Modular shelf configurations** that accommodate a broader range of products and boost storage density
*   **Pre-engineered safety features and integrated fire suppression**
*   Structural strengthening options providing**flexibility to meet seismic requirements**
*   **Reduced site readiness costs** through a unique leveling system that minimizes floor preparation

The new storage and buffering structure can be implemented as a retrofit to existing facilities or in new greenfield buildings, as part of the end-to-end Symbotic System.

“Customers are increasingly looking for flexible, ultra-high density warehouse automation to ensure the reliable flow of goods to consumers, and we’re seeing immediate traction with this new technology,” said Rick Cohen, Chairman and CEO of Symbotic. “Our next-generation storage structure represents a major leap forward in our mission to help customers improve efficiency, speed and resilience – all while accelerating return on investment.”

**Visual Assets**

Click to view two short videos showing the [benefits](https://vimeo.com/1105280880/967db461f9?ts=0&share=copy) of Symbotic’s next-generation storage technology, and an [installation overview](https://vimeo.com/1105281573/f7048c885f?ts=0&share=copy).

####

**ABOUT SYMBOTIC**

Symbotic is an automation technology leader reimagining the supply chain with its end-to-end, A.I.-powered robotic and software platform. Symbotic reinvents the warehouse as a strategic asset for the world’s largest retail, wholesale, and food & beverage companies. Applying next-generation technology, high-density storage and machine learning to solve today’s complex distribution challenges, Symbotic enables companies to move goods with unmatched speed, agility, accuracy and efficiency. As the backbone of commerce Symbotic transforms the flow of goods and the economics of the supply chain for its customers. For more information, visit [www.symbotic.com](http://www.symbotic.com/).

# FAQs ABOUT THE SKYPOD SYSTEM Q:  How many bins per hour can the system 

present per station? 

A:  400 - 500 bin presentations per hour 

Q:  What is the storage height of the rack? 

A:  36 feet (5 times the density of storage in standard shelving) 

Q:  Can I add pick stations? 

A:  Yes, one of the advantages of Exotec is the scalability 

Q:  Can I use a pick station for picking and replenishment? 

A:  Yes 

Q:  What is the average lead time for a system implementation? 

A:  Depending on the size, Exotec currently averages around a 6 to 8 month lead time 

Q:  Where is the largest Exotec installation currently implemented? 

A:  A site in Japan has 100k SKU locations and a throughput of 5,000 LPH 

Q:  Will Hy-Tek support the maintenance of 

the system? 

A:  Yes 

Q:  Is the Exotec solution scalable? 

A:  Yes 

Q:  Does Exotec have space for an internal 

sprinkler system? 

A:  Yes, the system has been designed to include a fire suppression system (if required) ABOUT THE SKYPOD ROBOT Q:  What is the carrying capacity of the 

Skypod? 

A:  66 lbs 

Q:  Are there multiple size bins available? 

A:  Yes 

Q:  Can I add Skypods? 

A:  Yes, one of the advantages of Exotec is the scalability 

Q:  How fast can the Skypod travel? 

A:  9 mph (on the ground and climbing the rack) 

Q:  What is the weight of a Skypod? 

A:  100lbs 

Q:  Battery type on the Skypod robots? 

A:  Lithium-Ion 

Q:  How long does the Skypod battery last per charge? 

A:  Opportunity charging is included in the systems function, so the system can operate 

24/7 

Q:  Does Exotec offer a leasing model for additional Skypods during peak season? 

A:  We are currently working on rolling out a leasing model to offer to customers ABOUT THE SKYPICKER Q:  What is the carrying capacity of the 

Skypicker? 

A:  2.2 lbs 

Q:  How fast can the Skypicker’s tool move? 

A:  4.5 mph 

Q:  How does the Skypicker identify items? 

A:  RGBD scanner 

Q:  How does the Skypicker grasp items? 

A:  Suction cup with pump 

Q:  How many lines per hour can the Skypicker 

present per station? 

A:  400 - 600 lines per hour 

Q:  What are the dimensions of a station? 

A:  13.12 x 13.12 x 9.84 ft 

Q:  What makes up the Skypicker station? 

A:  The robotic arm and order mover (allowing automatic and simultaneous preparation of 4 orders) 

See the Exotec system in action!
